drug_class: Dual endothelin receptor antagonist and angiotensin receptor blocker (ERA/ARB)
purpose: Sparsentan is used to help slow down kidney damage in adults with a kidney disease called IgA nephropathy (IgAN). It helps protect your kidneys by reducing protein in the urine, which is a sign of kidney stress. Your doctor may prescribe this to help keep your kidneys working as well as possible for as long as possible.
how_it_works: Your kidneys are being harmed by two things working against them: a chemical called endothelin and a hormone system called the renin-angiotensin system. Sparsentan blocks both of these at the same time, which helps relax and protect the tiny blood vessels in your kidneys. By doing both jobs in one pill, it reduces the strain on your kidneys and lowers the amount of protein leaking into your urine.
common_side_effects: Swelling in your hands, feet, or ankles; dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up); low blood pressure; stuffy or runny nose; tiredness; and stomach pain or discomfort.
warnings: This medication can cause serious birth defects — do not take it if you are pregnant, and use reliable birth control while taking it. You will need to enroll in a special safety program (called a REMS program) before starting this medication. It can also raise liver enzyme levels, so your doctor will check your liver with blood tests regularly. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-sparing medications unless your doctor says it is okay, as this drug can raise potassium levels in your blood.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 200 mg taken by mouth once daily. After about four weeks, your doctor will likely increase your dose to 400 mg once daily if you are tolerating it well. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
